target_customer: Adult consumers in California who want a low dose cannabis social drink instead of alcohol, sold through dispensaries
problem: Alcohol is the default social drink; California Dreamin offered all natural low dose cannabis sodas as a lighter alternative without couch lock.
business_model: Consumer packaged goods sold wholesale to licensed dispensaries

founders.name: Amy Bishop
founders.background_notes: From the YC bio. Other sources name this co-founder Amy Ludlum; the surname conflict is unresolved.

founders.name: Peter Bishop
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without a bio.

exit.reason: Cause not public; YC lists the company as Inactive and no closure announcement was found.

competitors.name: Lagunitas Hi-Fi Hops (with CannaCraft)
competitors.what: THC or CBD infused zero calorie sparkling water made by Lagunitas and sold by CannaCraft in California dispensaries
competitors.traction_then: Slated for California dispensary shelves in July 2018; cannabis drinks were 58 million dollars of US sales that year
competitors.funding_then: Backed by a large brewer and a licensed California manufacturer

technical_complexity.rationale: Beverage formulation with cannabis dosing consistency and testing, plus California licensing, but no novel technology; contract manufacturing was available.

defensibility.rationale: California licensing was a barrier to entry, but flavors and branding were copyable and a big brewer entered by mid 2018.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Lagunitas launched Hi-Fi Hops with CannaCraft in mid 2018; no source shows an acquisition of California Dreamin.

market_need_then: California legal recreational sales began in January 2018 and cannabis beverages were a small, fast growing category (58 million dollars US sales in 2018 per Arcview and BDS Analytics via Fortune).

branding.domain_note: Used drinkdreamin.com, a prefix domain rather than an exact match; it returned 503 when fetched (2026-11).

identity.visual_style: Funky bottle with fruit flavored sodas; branding and packaging by CODO Design
identity.voice_and_tone: Social and light, with the line 'Enjoy a light, social high' and 'we don't want couch lock'

branding.brand_signature: The 'light, social high' positioning as an alternative to beer
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch covered the launch as 'marijuana soda startup wants to replace booze' (2018-03-19) and Trend Hunter and BeverageDaily also covered it.

brand_strength.rationale: Good launch press and a clear social drink positioning with professional packaging, but no evidence of a lasting following; the product was also sold under the parent name Seven Cities Bev Co.

outcome_analysis: California Dreamin launched cannabis sodas at YC Demo Day in March 2018 and announced 2.3 million dollars in funding. The cause of its becoming inactive is not public, so failure factors are left empty. Strong competition from a large brewer with a licensed manufacturer arrived by mid 2018, and California tightened THC beverage rules later, but no source ties these to this company.
notes: The 2.3 million round is from BevNET (seen only in a search summary; the page returned 403), with CB Insights giving 2.42M total, so another small amount is unitemised. The round date is given only as 2018. Co-founder surname conflict: YC page says Amy Bishop, other outlets say Amy Ludlum. Competitor Hi-Fi Hops source is dated June 2018, a few months after the March 2018 demo day. Company website returned 503.
